page.text:
John von Neumann provided a canonical set-theoretic realization of the
natural numbers. In this construction, zero is the empty set $\emptyset$,
and each successive number is the set of all numbers preceding it:
$0 = \emptyset$, $1 = \{0\} = \{\emptyset\}$, $2 = \{0, 1\}$, and in
general $S(n) = n \cup \{n\}$. This elegant encoding makes the membership
relation $\in$ coincide with the strict order $<$ on the naturals.
